 - When using `find -regex` with alternation, put the longest alternative first. Example: use `'.*\.\(tsx\|ts\)'` not `'.*\.\(ts\|tsx\)'` — the second form silently skips `.tsx` files.


# Committing changes with git

Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:

You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. The numbered steps below indicate which commands should be batched in parallel.

Git Safety Protocol:
- NEVER update the git config
- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions 
- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it
- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it
- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit
- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries
- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the Bash tool:
  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.
  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.
  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.
2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:
  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).
  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files
  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"
  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

And even absent that signal, it's still fine to stop when you're genuinely blocked — unclear direction, missing input, a decision only they can make.

Before any command that could discard uncommitted work — `git checkout`/`restore`/`reset`/`clean`, `rm -rf` in the repo, restoring from a snapshot — run `git status` first and stash (with `-u` for untracked) or commit anything that's there. When staging or committing, review what's included (`git status` after a broad `git add`), and if you see anything suspicious that might reveal secrets — even if the filename looks innocuous — double-check the file's contents before pushing.
</system-reminder>

97	 * bleed this component edge-to-edge on mobile/tablet — without forwarding it, this branch would

102	 * screenshots) — this genuinely renders edge-to-edge on all three surfaces.
103	 *
104	 * **The See-Full-History link, added 2026-09-08 — previously a stated "not yet built" gap on
105	 * every caller.** `seeAllHref`/`seeAllLabel` are computed here, once, rather than by

107	 * `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount()` (app/hooks — 2/3/5 per breakpoint), matching the AC's own

109	 * Question 1, reopened 2026-09-07 after the original flat->5 reading was found to misread that AC

111	 * was `useBreakpointValue(RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS)`** — that resolves the "Desktop"
112	 * step at this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px), but the rail's own card-width styling

114	 * between 1024–1280px (confirmed live, Marcel: ~1277px showed the row styled for 5 cards, only 3

116	 * `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`'s own docblock for the full incident and why a plain
117	 * `useBreakpointValue` object can't express this threshold at all. No ResizeObserver — this hook
118	 * reads the current breakpoint only. `seeAllHref` is site/locale-prefixed via `useMultiSite`'s own
119	 * `buildUrl` — this container builds the prefix, never the rail itself (AGENTS.md's Multi-site

126	import React, { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
127	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
128	import { useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';
129	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
130	import type { BoxProps } from '@chakra-ui/react';
131	import { Box, Button } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
132	import ProductScroller from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller';
133	import useEinstein from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein';
134	import useDataCloud from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-datacloud';
135	import { useCurrentCustomer } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-customer';

149	// Zimmermann's own constants — NOT the base package above. RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE only exists
150	// here; importing it from the base package instead compiles (that module has no real type
151	// declarations, so any named import type-checks as `any`) but is `undefined` at runtime —
152	// confirmed the hard way via a failing test before this was split out.
153	import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE } from 'app/constants';
154	import { useShopperCustomersMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
155	// Relative, not the base package path — .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an
156	// already-overridden component from a new component": .storybook/main.js and vitest.config.ts
157	// don't load the overrides resolver, so a base-path import here would silently story/test the
158	// unstyled base component instead of this override.

160	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
161	import { selectRecentlyViewedCard } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedCard';
162	import type { RecentlyViewedCard, RecentlyViewedProduct } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedCard';
163	import { useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount';
164	
165	/**
166	 * The See-Full-History link's own accessible label. Not in this file's existing message set (it
167	 * had none before this step) because nothing here owned any copy of its own until now — `title`
168	 * has always been each caller's own responsibility (see the Recently-Viewed branch below), and
169	 * this is the one piece of copy this container itself needs.
170	 */

172	  seeFullHistory: {
173	    id: 'recommended_products.link.see_full_history',
174	    defaultMessage: 'See Full History',
175	  },
176	});
177	
178	/**
179	 * The one field this file reads off a recommendation-context product. A real
180	 * commerce-sdk-isomorphic Product shape underlies it, but @salesforce/retail-react-app's
181	 * useEinstein/ProductScroller ship untyped (vendor.d.ts's wildcard), so this is narrowed
182	 * to exactly the field touched here rather than invented more broadly (AGENTS.md > Type
183	 * Definitions: hand-roll only the genuinely unexported shape actually used).
184	 */
185	type RecommendedProduct = { productId?: string };
186	
187	export type RecommendedProductsProps = {
188	  /* The title to appear above the product scroller */
189	  title?: ReactNode;
190	
191	  /* The zone to request */
192	  zone?: string;
193	
194	  /* The recommender to request */
195	  recommender?: string;
196	
197	  /* The products to use for recommendation context */
198	  products?: readonly Record<string, unknown>[];
199	
200	  /* Callback to determine if the component should fetch results */
201	  shouldFetch?: () => boolean;
202	
203	  // Index signature for the `...props` passthrough to ProductScroller (itself untyped — see
204	  // vendor.d.ts). Without it, the destructured rest types as `{}` instead of accepting arbitrary
205	  // passthrough, which is the base file's actual intent: forwarding whatever else the caller
206	  // passes.
207	  [key: string]: unknown;
208	};

210	/**
211	 * A component for fetching and rendering product recommendations from the Einstein API
212	 * by a zone or a recommender name.
213	 */
214	const RecommendedProducts = ({
215	  zone,
216	  recommender,
217	  products,
218	  title,
219	  shouldFetch,
220	  ...props
221	}: RecommendedProductsProps) => {
222	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getZoneRecommendations, getRecommendations, sendClickReco, sendViewReco } =
223	    useEinstein();
224	  const { data: customer } = useCurrentCustomer();
225	  const { customerId } = customer;
226	  const { data: wishlist } = useWishList();
227	  const dataCloud = useDataCloud();
228	
229	  const createCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('createCustomerProductListItem');
230	  const deleteCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('deleteCustomerProductListItem');
231	  const toast = useToast();
232	  const navigate = useNavigation();
233	  const intl = useIntl();
234	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's own consumer uses
235	  // (product-list/index.tsx): passed into the mapper rather than formatted there, keeping that
236	  // mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
237	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
238	
239	  const ref = useRef();
240	  const isOnScreen = useIntersectionObserver(ref, { useOnce: true });
241	  const [_products, setProducts] = useState(products);
242	  // Cart-exclusion check (2026-09-10, Marcel: "no recently viewed on cart" — a standing product
243	  // decision, not an Einstein-not-deployed-yet placeholder). Cart has no Zimmermann override
244	  // (no overrides/app/pages/cart/ at all) — its base page imports this same overridden component
245	  // and passes `recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED}`, which resolves to the
246	  // exact same string as PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED (confirmed identical,
247	  // node_modules/.../constants.js:154-160), so the recommender check below cannot tell the two
248	  // apart by value alone. `.endsWith('/cart')`, not an exact match — AGENTS.md's Multi-site
249	  // section: a real storefront path is locale/site-prefixed (e.g. `/en-GB/cart`), so an exact
250	  // `=== '/cart'` would only ever match the default site.
251	  const location = useLocation();
252	  const isCartPage = location.pathname.endsWith('/cart');
253	  // The See-Full-History trigger threshold, resolved for whichever breakpoint is actually
254	  // current. Also unconditional per rules of hooks; only meaningful inside the Recently-Viewed
255	  // branch below, same as `useLocation()` immediately above (whose derived `isCartPage` is also
256	  // only meaningful there). Reads the current breakpoint only — no ResizeObserver, no runtime DOM
257	  // measurement, matching the AC's own viewport-relative "exceeds the visible rail width" wording
258	  // (Open Question 1). See the module docblock's own "See-Full-History link" section for why this
259	  // is no longer a plain `useBreakpointValue` call.
260	  const visibleCardCount = useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount();
261	  // `buildUrl` site/locale-prefixes an internal path (e.g. `/en-GB/recently-viewed` on a non-AU
262	  // storefront) — AGENTS.md's Multi-site section: never assume routing. The rail itself must not
263	  // build this prefix; this container does it once, here.
264	  const { buildUrl } = useMultiSite();
265	
266	  useEffect(() => {
267	    // Check if the component should fetch results or not. This is useful
268	    // when you are still waiting on additional data, like `products`.
269	    if (typeof shouldFetch === 'function' && !shouldFetch()) {
270	      return;
271	    }
272	
273	    // Fetch either zone or recommender, but not both. If a zone and recommender
274	    // name are both provided, `zone` takes precendence.
275	    if (zone) {
276	      getZoneRecommendations(zone, _products);
277	      return;
278	    }
279	    if (recommender) {
280	      getRecommendations(recommender, _products);
281	      return;
282	    }
283	  }, [zone, recommender, _products]);
284	
285	  useEffect(() => {
286	    // This is an optimization that eliminates superfluous rerenders/fetching by
287	    // keeping a copy of the `products` array prop in state for shallow comparison.
288	    if (!Array.isArray(products)) {
289	      return;
290	    }
291	    if (products.length !== _products?.length || !products.every((val, index) => val === _products?.[index])) {
292	      setProducts(products);
293	    }
294	  }, [products]);
295	
296	  useEffect(() => {
297	    if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs) {
298	      sendViewReco(
299	        {
300	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
301	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
302	        },
303	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
304	      );
305	      dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations(
306	        {
307	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
308	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
309	        },
310	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
311	      );
312	    }
313	  }, [isOnScreen, recommendations]);
314	
315	  // SFCC-83 — Recently Viewed only. Every other recommender falls through to the unchanged
316	  // ProductScroller branch below. This branch sits ahead of the base dead-check below (see this
317	  // file's own module docblock, point 3, for why that no longer strictly matters but is kept
318	  // anyway) — every path inside this `if` returns on its own, so it never falls through to that
319	  // dead-check or the ProductScroller return regardless. Every other recommender is unaffected:
320	  // they still hit the exact same dead-check + ProductScroller path below, unchanged, just after
321	  // this check now short-circuits past them when it applies.
322	  if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
323	    // Cart exclusion (2026-09-10, Marcel) — see the isCartPage constant's own comment above for
324	    // why this can't be expressed as a distinct recommender value. No rail, no title, no
325	    // placeholder — same treatment as the empty-state gate below, just for a different reason.
326	    if (isCartPage) {
327	      return null;
328	    }
329	
330	    // AC 8's empty-state gate, now against Einstein's own recs directly (build plan step E1) —
331	    // see this file's own module docblock for why this one check covers both the loading case
332	    // (`recs` undefined until `getRecommendations` resolves) and the true zero-history case. No
333	    // rail, no title, no placeholder.
334	    if (!recommendations?.recs?.length) {
335	      return null;
336	    }
337	
338	    // `recommendations.recs` is `useEinstein()`'s own untyped (`any`) result — like the
339	    // `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks elsewhere in this file that already read off it, the
340	    // mapping callback below needs an explicit parameter-type annotation to satisfy
341	    // `noImplicitAny`. `RecentlyViewedProduct` (recentlyViewedCard.ts's own alias for
342	    // `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`) is reused here rather than a hand-rolled inline shape, since
343	    // it already names every field `selectRecentlyViewedCard` reads, and this input is a strict
344	    // superset of it (see the module docblock above).
345	    const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = recommendations.recs
346	      .map((product: RecentlyViewedProduct) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice))
347	      .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
348	      .map(
349	        (card: RecentlyViewedCard): ZimmProductCardProps => ({
350	          ...card,
351	          // Inert for this variation — ZimmProductCardContent never mounts when
352	          // variation: 'recentlyViewed' (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's
353	          // VARIATION_CONFIG.showContent). 'h3' matches the one other established value for
354	          // this same required field (product-list/productListCardMapper.ts).
355	          headingLevel: 'h3',
356	          variation: 'recentlyViewed',
357	        }),
358	      );
359	
360	    // The See-Full-History link, finally wired in (was a stated "not yet built" gap on every
361	    // caller until now). Triggers when the shopper has more recently-viewed products
362	    // than fit in view at the *current* breakpoint — matching the AC's own "exceeds the visible
363	    // rail width" wording, which is viewport-relative, not a flat count. Compared against
364	    // `cards.length` (the full, unsliced count this container just built from Einstein's own
365	    // `recommendations.recs` — no client-side cap, build plan step E4 Open Question 4), not the
366	    // rail's own internal 5-item render slice, since the question is "does more exist than is
367	    // visible", not "did we cap the render".
368	    const showSeeAllLink = cards.length > visibleCardCount;
369	
370	    return (
371	      // Ref-attachment point — see the module docblock's own isOnScreen/forwardRef note above for
372	      // why this wrapper exists at all. `{...props}` forwards the caller's own layout props (e.g.
373	      // PDP's `mx={{base: -4, md: -8, lg: 0}}`, Cart's `mx={{base: -4, sm: -6, lg: 0}}`) exactly
374	      // as the ProductScroller branch below already does — without it, this branch would render
375	      // inset inside the page's normal content padding while every sibling rail on the same page
376	      // bleeds edge-to-edge, and zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own card-width math (e.g.
377	      // 201x2=402) assumes the full viewport width is actually available. `title` is passed
378	      // straight through with no `recommendations?.displayMessage` fallback — this component owns
379	      // no copy of its own for this branch (build plan A5/A6): the real title always comes from
380	      // the caller, regardless of whether Einstein's own `displayMessage` is present.
381	      <Box ref={ref} {...(props as BoxProps)}>
382	        <ZimmRecentlyViewedRail
383	          title={title}
384	          cards={cards}
385	          seeAllHref={showSeeAllLink ? buildUrl(RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE) : undefined}
386	          seeAllLabel={showSeeAllLink ? intl.formatMessage(messages.seeFullHistory) : undefined}
387	        />
388	      </Box>
389	    );
390	  }
391	
392	  // The component should remove itself altogether if it has no recommendations
393	  // and we aren't loading any.
394	  if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) {
395	    return null;
396	  }
397	
398	  // TODO: DRY this handler when intl provider is available globally
399	  const addItemToWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
400	    try {
401	      if (!wishlist || !customerId) {
402	        return;
403	      }
404	      await createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
405	        parameters: {
406	          listId: wishlist.id,
407	          customerId,
408	        },
409	        body: {
410	          quantity: 1,

249	  // array is the direct equivalent -- `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` is off repo-wide

252	  // home/index.tsx's own `useEffect(() => { einstein.sendViewPage(pathname); }, []);`.
253	  useEffect(() => {
254	    getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED);
255	  }, []);

258	  // consumers already use: formatPrice is injected into the mapper rather than formatted inside
259	  // it, keeping that mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
260	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string): string =>

262	
263	  // Size-aware Add to Bag (2026-09-09 full-parity-with-PLP build) -- keyed by product id rather

268	  // full control) -- touching that organism's contract to add one would be a bigger, cross-cutting
269	  // change than this fix calls for (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5: never refactor upward). A single
270	  // id-keyed map at this container achieves the same "each card remembers its own selected size"
271	  // result without touching the Grid at all.
272	  const [selectedSizeChipValues, setSelectedSizeChipValues] = useState<Record<string, string | undefined>>({});
273

275	    addItemToNewOrExistingBasket([{ productId: orderableProductId, price, quantity: 1 }])
276	      .then(() => toast({ title: intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToBag), status: 'success' }))

content.text:
Branch confirmed: `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein` (not `develop`/`main`) — proceeded.

## Fix 1 — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`

**Consequence (was):** a returning shopper whose entire history is now stale (every product deleted/offline) saw a blank page — no grid, no "you haven't viewed anything" message, nothing.

**Mechanism:** the render gate checked `recs.length` (raw Einstein count) instead of `cards.length` (count after the null-mapping filter). Recs non-empty but all mapped to `null` → gate says "populated" → renders `<ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid cards={[]} />`, which is documented to render `null` for an empty array. The empty-state branch never got a chance to fire because its own condition was also `recs.length === 0` (false).

**Fix:** both ternary conditions now read `cards.length` (`index.tsx:329` and `:368`). `isLoading` handling and the `recs`→`cards` derivation are untouched — `cards` is already a synchronous, same-render `.map().filter()` over `recs`, so no new async race is introduced. Also corrected the docblock's "Empty-state gate" paragraph (`:191-211`), which asserted this exact bug was "not solved here, not new here" — that claim is now false, so I rewrote it rather than leave stale documentation next to the fix that disproves it.

**Test evidence** (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx`):
- Added the required new case (`:258-280`): recs non-empty, every rec maps to `null` → asserts `recently-viewed-empty` renders, grid stub doesn't.
- **Proved it, not just asserted it:** reverted the gate to `recs.length` (`Edit` → `npx vitest run` → confirmed exactly 1 failure, this new test, rendering the grid stub instead of the empty state) → restored the fix → confirmed 12/12 pass again. Both runs shown in full above.
- Also had to correct one pre-existing test, `'renders a real h1 ... in the populated branch'` (`:183-204`): its fixture set `mockSelectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.mockReturnValue(null)` with non-empty recs — i.e. it was accidentally already exercising the exact all-null-mapped scenario this fix targets. It kept "passing" throughout because its only assertion was "does the h1 render" (true regardless of branch), so it never actually caught the bug even though it was sitting right on top of it. I changed its mock to return real cards so the scenario now genuinely matches its own "populated branch" name, and added an assertion that the grid stub renders. This is a mechanical correction inside the file already named for this fix, not a new judgment call.

## Fix 2 — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`

**Consequence (was):** an Einstein network call fired on every Cart page load for a result the component was already guaranteed to throw away (the render branch returns `null` unconditionally on Cart for this recommender).

**Fix:** added the guard at the top of the fetch effect (`:267-276`) — `if (isCartPage && recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) return;` before the `getRecommendations` call — and added `isCartPage` to the effect's dependency array (`:295`). No other recommender/route combination is touched by this condition. Also corrected one now-inaccurate sentence in an adjacent comment (`:254-260`) that said `isCartPage` was "only meaningful" in the render branch below — it's now also read in the fetch effect above that branch.

## Verification

```
npx tsc --noEmit    → clean, no output, exit 0
npm run test -- --run → Test Files  1 failed | 84 passed (85)
                         Tests       1 failed | 1305 passed (1306)
```

85 files / 1306 tests matches the expected baseline+1 exactly. `recipeGuards.test.ts` (the styling gate) passed, unaffected — expected, since neither fix touches styling.

`git status --porcelain` confirms exactly 3 files changed, no others:
```
M overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx
M overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.test.tsx
M overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx
```

## The one failure — stopping here, not deciding it myself

`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx:281-308` (`'on the Cart route, renders null even when recs has items'`) now fails:

```
AssertionError: expected "spy" to be called with arguments: [ 'viewed-recently-einstein', …(1) ]
Number of calls: 0
```

This is the direct, correct consequence of Fix 2 — the test's own comment (`:303-306`) explicitly pinned the old "wasted call" as accepted behavior ("Documented here rather than left as an untested assumption"), and Fix 2 removes exactly that call. This is effectively confirmation the guard works, seen from the test side.

I have not touched this file — it wasn't named in either fix's manifest, and per my instructions I stop and report rather than silently editing a file outside scope, even when the fix is mechanical. The minimal correction, for whoever ratifies it, is to flip the final assertion in that test to `expect(mockGetRecommendations).not.toHaveBeenCalled();` and update the comment above it (currently calls this an "accepted wasted call" — no longer true). That's a one-line + one-comment change, in the same file, same test, nothing else in it needs to move.

**Report is honest, not smoothed over:** the actual run is 1305 passed / 1 failed, not a clean 1306/1306 — I'm not rounding that off.

## What Marcel is missing

The pre-existing "populated branch" h1 test (recentlyViewed) was already sitting on top of this exact all-stale-history bug before either of us touched it this session — it just couldn't see it, because its assertion only checked "does an h1 render" rather than "did the right branch render." Worth a quick sweep for other tests in this suite whose assertions are narrower than the scenario they set up — that's exactly the shape of bug that survives review because the test technically passes.
